title: String Interleaving
statement:
Check whether a third string can be formed by weaving two strings together without reordering either one.

Contract
- All three arguments are non-null and may be empty; characters compare exactly (case-sensitive).
- `merged` is an interleaving when its characters can be split into two subsequences that spell `first` and `second`, using every character of `merged` exactly once.
- Characters taken from `first` keep their order, and so do those from `second`; the two strings may alternate in any pattern.
- Return `false` immediately when the lengths do not add up. Three empty strings are an interleaving.

Examples
- `isInterleaving("ab", "ac", "acab")` returns `true`: take `a`, `c` from the second string, then `a`, `b` from the first.
- `isInterleaving("ab", "cd", "acbe")` returns `false`: `e` appears in neither string.
- `isInterleaving("", "xyz", "xyz")` returns `true`: everything comes from the second string.
hints: Whether merged[k] can come from either string depends only on how many characters of each string have been used so far.

Let reachable[i][j] mean the first i characters of `first` and first j of `second` can weave into the first i + j characters of `merged`. Fill it from smaller prefixes: step i or step j when the character matches.

Row i of the table only needs row i - 1, so a single row of length |second| + 1 is enough. Intended complexity: O(|first| * |second|) time and O(|second|) extra space; with both strings of length n that is O(n^2) time and O(n) space.
inputSyntax: Input: three words (first second merged), for example: ab ac acab
